questions.topic: Maximum temporary absence of a sole pharmacist
questions.trigger: A pharmacy is staffed by only one pharmacist. During the six-hour work period, the pharmacist proposes a 35-minute meal break outside the prescription area but on the premises, with the pharmacy remaining open. All drug-security conditions are met. What adjustment is required under the temporary-absence rule?
questions.legal_decision: Shorten the temporary absence to no more than 30 minutes per six hours, or arrange compliant pharmacist coverage.
questions.critical_exception: Remaining on the premises and maintaining security do not waive the time limit.
questions.counterfactual_flip: An otherwise compliant 25-minute absence within the six-hour period would not exceed the stated time limit.
questions.stem: A pharmacy is staffed by only one pharmacist. During the six-hour work period, the pharmacist proposes a 35-minute meal break outside the prescription area but on the premises, with the pharmacy remaining open. All drug-security conditions are met. What adjustment is required under the temporary-absence rule?

choices.text: Permit 35 minutes because the pharmacist remains in the building.
choices.why: Incorrect. Remaining on the premises does not remove the time limit.

choices.text: Permit 35 minutes because technicians will continue routine work.
choices.why: Incorrect. Technical duties do not enlarge the exception.

choices.text: Limit the absence to 30 minutes or arrange compliant pharmacist coverage.
choices.why: Correct. The sole-pharmacist temporary-absence rule limits the absence to 30 minutes per six hours.

choices.text: Move the meal off the premises to avoid the limit.
choices.why: Incorrect. This exception requires remaining on the premises.

choices.text: Permit any duration if controlled substances are secure.
choices.why: Incorrect. The security condition does not replace the duration limit.

questions.topic: Manager responsibility for adequate staffing despite legal ratio
questions.trigger: A pharmacy meets the applicable numerical pharmacist-to-support-personnel ratio. Repeated workflow reviews nevertheless demonstrate inadequate staffing that delays necessary safety checks and creates risks for patients. Which response reflects the Manager of Record's duty?
questions.legal_decision: Plan and maintain adequate staffing promoting patient safety; monitor and enforce appropriate procedures.
questions.critical_exception: Compliance with a numerical maximum ratio does not by itself establish adequate staffing.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the staffing and processes actually supported patient safety, the stated inadequacy would not exist.
questions.stem: A pharmacy meets the applicable numerical pharmacist-to-support-personnel ratio. Repeated workflow reviews nevertheless demonstrate inadequate staffing that delays necessary safety checks and creates risks for patients. Which response reflects the Manager of Record's duty?

choices.text: Take no action unless a patient has already suffered an injury.
choices.why: Incorrect. The duty is preventive, not conditioned on actual harm.

choices.text: Delegate the staffing duty entirely to the corporate scheduler.
choices.why: Incorrect. Corporate assistance does not remove the MOR's assigned responsibility.

choices.text: Treat the numerical ratio as the sole staffing requirement.
choices.why: Incorrect. The MOR also has an affirmative patient-safety staffing responsibility.

choices.text: Address the documented staffing inadequacy and monitor the resulting procedures.
choices.why: Correct. Adequate staffing and effective procedures are express MOR responsibilities.

choices.text: Reduce the number of pharmacist checks to match available staffing.
choices.why: Incorrect. The MOR must maintain professional practice standards rather than eliminate required checks.

critical_error_options.reason: The MOR must maintain professional practice standards rather than eliminate required checks.

questions.topic: DEA registration and employed dispensing pharmacist
questions.trigger: A Massachusetts-licensed pharmacist is employed by a retail pharmacy holding the required current state licenses and DEA pharmacy registration. The pharmacist acts in the usual course of professional practice but has no individual DEA registration. Under the federal rule on persons entitled to fill controlled prescriptions, which conclusion is correct?
questions.legal_decision: Employment in a properly registered pharmacy satisfies the federal registration pathway for ordinary pharmacist filling.
questions.critical_exception: The rule distinguishes pharmacists filling prescriptions from practitioners prescribing under individual registration.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the pharmacy were not registered and no other authorized registration pathway applied, the stated employment would not satisfy the federal rule.
questions.stem: A Massachusetts-licensed pharmacist is employed by a retail pharmacy holding the required current state licenses and DEA pharmacy registration. The pharmacist acts in the usual course of professional practice but has no individual DEA registration. Under the federal rule on persons entitled to fill controlled prescriptions, which conclusion is correct?

choices.text: The pharmacist may fill only Schedule VI prescriptions.
choices.why: Incorrect. The federal rule permits controlled prescription filling within registered pharmacy practice.

choices.text: The pharmacist's personal state license alone would permit dispensing at any unregistered pharmacy.
choices.why: Incorrect. The federal registration conditions still apply.

choices.text: The pharmacist may fill federally controlled prescriptions when all applicable dispensing conditions are met.
choices.why: Correct. The regulation permits the registered-pharmacy employment pathway.

choices.text: The pharmacist may use the pharmacy registration to write independent controlled prescriptions for any patient.
choices.why: Incorrect. This rule authorizes filling, not general prescriptive authority.

choices.text: The pharmacist must obtain an individual DEA registration for every Schedule II prescription filled.
choices.why: Incorrect. A pharmacist employed by a registered pharmacy may fill controlled prescriptions.

questions.topic: Pharmacist licensure application fees after Board review
questions.trigger: The Board has reviewed and acted upon an application for pharmacist licensure by examination. The applicant withdraws after the decision and requests the return of the application fees already submitted. Assume no special fee waiver or refund authority applies. What does 247 CMR 3.01 provide?
questions.legal_decision: Fees submitted for a pharmacist licensure application reviewed and acted upon by the Board are nonrefundable.
questions.critical_exception: The relevant condition is Board review and action, not whether licensure was granted.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A fee waiver authorized separately must be considered under its own conditions.
questions.stem: The Board has reviewed and acted upon an application for pharmacist licensure by examination. The applicant withdraws after the decision and requests the return of the application fees already submitted. Assume no special fee waiver or refund authority applies. What does 247 CMR 3.01 provide?

choices.text: The fees must be transferred to another state's Board.
choices.why: Incorrect. The Massachusetts regulation imposes no such duty.

choices.text: Fees are refundable whenever an applicant is denied licensure.
choices.why: Incorrect. The rule does not make denial an automatic refund event.

choices.text: The Board must refund all fees whenever an applicant withdraws.
choices.why: Incorrect. Withdrawal does not override the stated nonrefundability.

choices.text: The fees are nonrefundable once the Board has reviewed and acted on the application.
choices.why: Correct. The section expressly establishes nonrefundability in that circumstance.

choices.text: The fees must be converted into continuing education credit.
choices.why: Incorrect. Application fees do not constitute CE credit.

questions.topic: Board-approved home-study CE program design
questions.trigger: An organization applying for Board approval of a mediated home-study pharmacy CE program proposes only recorded lectures without learner responses, feedback, completion testing or references for continued study. Which changes address the specified mediated-instruction criteria? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
questions.legal_decision: Provide active learner response and feedback, progress/completion testing, and bibliography.
questions.critical_exception: Passive viewing alone does not meet the specified criteria for Board-approved mediated programs.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A program meeting these criteria must still satisfy the other provider and program requirements.
questions.stem: An organization applying for Board approval of a mediated home-study pharmacy CE program proposes only recorded lectures without learner responses, feedback, completion testing or references for continued study. Which changes address the specified mediated-instruction criteria? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Classify the program as live merely because the videos contain a faculty member.
choices.why: Incorrect. A recording does not establish direct live faculty-participant interaction.

choices.text: Provide a bibliography for further study.
choices.why: Correct. The regulation identifies this resource.

choices.text: Replace the assessment with a tuition receipt only.
choices.why: Incorrect. Payment does not verify learning or completion.

choices.text: Include activities requiring learner responses with feedback.
choices.why: Correct. The mediated-instruction criteria require learner involvement and feedback.

choices.text: Add a test to assess progress and verify program completion.
choices.why: Correct. A test serves the stated verification purpose.

questions.topic: Technician licensure education while enrolled in high school
questions.trigger: An 18-year-old applicant is currently enrolled in a program leading to a high school diploma, has Board-accepted national technician certification, and satisfies all other Massachusetts technician eligibility and application requirements. Which conclusion follows from the education criterion?
questions.legal_decision: Current enrollment in a qualifying diploma or equivalent program can satisfy the educational requirement.
questions.critical_exception: Graduation is not the only permissible way to meet the education criterion.
questions.counterfactual_flip: An applicant with neither graduation/equivalent nor current qualifying enrollment would not meet this criterion.
questions.stem: An 18-year-old applicant is currently enrolled in a program leading to a high school diploma, has Board-accepted national technician certification, and satisfies all other Massachusetts technician eligibility and application requirements. Which conclusion follows from the education criterion?

choices.text: National certification removes the age and education requirements.
choices.why: Incorrect. The qualification route does not waive the other eligibility criteria.

choices.text: The applicant must wait until age 21.
choices.why: Incorrect. The technician minimum age is 18.

choices.text: The applicant can meet the education criterion through current enrollment.
choices.why: Correct. The rule permits graduation, equivalent education, or qualifying current enrollment.

choices.text: The applicant must already possess a diploma despite current qualifying enrollment.
choices.why: Incorrect. The education criterion expressly allows current qualifying enrollment.

choices.text: The applicant may work as a technician immediately without issuance of a license.
choices.why: Incorrect. A valid Board-issued technician license is still required.

questions.topic: Schedule classification of a barbiturate by dosage form
questions.trigger: Which federal and Massachusetts classifications are correct for ordinary single-ingredient pentobarbital injection and a pentobarbital suppository dosage form specifically FDA-approved for marketing only as a suppository, assuming no other exception applies?
questions.legal_decision: Pentobarbital injection is Schedule II; the specified suppository is Schedule III.
questions.critical_exception: The narrow dosage-form exception does not reschedule every pentobarbital formulation.
questions.counterfactual_flip: Without the specified suppository exception, the ordinary Schedule II listing applies.
questions.stem: Which federal and Massachusetts classifications are correct for ordinary single-ingredient pentobarbital injection and a pentobarbital suppository dosage form specifically FDA-approved for marketing only as a suppository, assuming no other exception applies?

choices.text: Both are Schedule II without exception.
choices.why: Incorrect. The regulation expressly lists the specified suppository dosage form in Schedule III.

choices.text: Injection II; qualifying suppository III.
choices.why: Correct. The general Schedule II listing is subject to the particular Schedule III suppository exception.

choices.text: Both are Schedule IV.
choices.why: Incorrect. Neither of the described formulations belongs to Schedule IV.

choices.text: Both are Massachusetts Schedule VI only.
choices.why: Incorrect. Both are federally scheduled in the described circumstances.

choices.text: Injection III; qualifying suppository II.
choices.why: Incorrect. The classifications are reversed.

questions.topic: Pain-management training prerequisite excludes veterinarians
questions.trigger: A Massachusetts physician and a veterinarian each prescribe controlled substances within their lawful practice. A licensing officer reviews the specific pain-management and opioid-risk training prerequisite in M.G.L. c. 94C, § 18(e). Which statement correctly describes the scope of that provision?
questions.legal_decision: The statutory training prerequisite applies to controlled-substance prescribers except veterinarians.
questions.critical_exception: The veterinarian exception concerns this training provision, not a blanket exemption from controlled-substance law.
questions.counterfactual_flip: Other applicable veterinary licensing or continuing education rules may still impose separate obligations.
questions.stem: A Massachusetts physician and a veterinarian each prescribe controlled substances within their lawful practice. A licensing officer reviews the specific pain-management and opioid-risk training prerequisite in M.G.L. c. 94C, § 18(e). Which statement correctly describes the scope of that provision?

choices.text: The veterinarian must complete the training but the physician is exempt.
choices.why: Incorrect. The stated exception is for veterinarians, not physicians.

choices.text: The veterinarian's exception eliminates DEA and other prescribing requirements.
choices.why: Incorrect. The exception does not eliminate unrelated registration or prescribing law.

choices.text: The physician is covered; veterinarians are expressly excepted from this specific prerequisite.
choices.why: Correct. The statutory exception expressly excludes veterinarians.

choices.text: Neither must complete the training unless prescribing a Schedule II opioid.
choices.why: Incorrect. The provision refers to practitioners prescribing controlled substances, subject to the express exception.

choices.text: Both practitioners are exempt because they hold professional licenses.
choices.why: Incorrect. The training is a prerequisite for covered practitioners obtaining or renewing licenses.

questions.topic: Quantity exception for an implantable infusion pump
questions.trigger: Two otherwise lawful prescriptions request a 60-day supply of a Schedule II opioid. Prescription X is for an ordinary oral opioid regimen for chronic pain. Prescription Y is specifically for use in an implantable infusion pump. Assume no separate statutory restriction or clinical obstacle. Which single-fill quantity conclusions are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
questions.legal_decision: The ordinary opioid remains subject to the 30-day single-fill ceiling; the implantable-pump prescription is within the specified 90-day category.
questions.critical_exception: The exception turns on the intended implantable infusion pump, not simply the opioid's clinical use for pain.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If Y were instead an ordinary oral opioid prescription, the pump exception would not apply.
questions.stem: Two otherwise lawful prescriptions request a 60-day supply of a Schedule II opioid. Prescription X is for an ordinary oral opioid regimen for chronic pain. Prescription Y is specifically for use in an implantable infusion pump. Assume no separate statutory restriction or clinical obstacle. Which single-fill quantity conclusions are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Prescription X is subject to the ordinary 30-day single-fill maximum.
choices.why: Correct. The stated use does not fall within the listed 90-day categories.

choices.text: Both automatically qualify for 90 days because chronic pain is present.
choices.why: Incorrect. Chronic pain alone is not a listed 90-day single-fill category.

choices.text: Prescription Y can fall within the implantable infusion pump 90-day maximum.
choices.why: Correct. Implantable infusion pumps are a specified exception.

choices.text: The pump must be treated exactly like any ordinary oral opioid for this quantity provision.
choices.why: Incorrect. The statute distinguishes the implantable pump category.

choices.text: The pump exception creates Schedule II refill authority.
choices.why: Incorrect. The quantity exception does not repeal the Schedule II refill prohibition.

questions.topic: Same-state prescribing-only office and separate DEA registration
questions.trigger: A physician holds a current DEA registration at a Massachusetts practice location. The physician opens another office in Massachusetts used only for issuing controlled-substance prescriptions. No controlled-substance stock is kept there, and controlled substances are neither administered nor otherwise dispensed there as a regular part of practice. Assume the separate office meets all Massachusetts requirements. What is the federal DEA registration consequence?
questions.legal_decision: The described prescribing-only office does not require a separate DEA registration under the federal exception.
questions.critical_exception: The other registered location must be in the same state, no supplies may be maintained, and administration or other dispensing must not occur as a regular part of practice.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the office regularly administered controlled substances from on-site stock, the prescribing-only office exception would no longer apply.
questions.stem: A physician holds a current DEA registration at a Massachusetts practice location. The physician opens another office in Massachusetts used only for issuing controlled-substance prescriptions. No controlled-substance stock is kept there, and controlled substances are neither administered nor otherwise dispensed there as a regular part of practice. Assume the separate office meets all Massachusetts requirements. What is the federal DEA registration consequence?

choices.text: A separate DEA registration is required for every office from which a controlled prescription is issued, without exception.
choices.why: Incorrect. Federal law provides a specific same-state prescribing-only office exception.

choices.text: The office qualifies for the exception to a separate DEA registration under the stated conditions.
choices.why: Correct. The registered location is in the same state and the other office has no stock or regular administration or other dispensing.

choices.text: The physician may maintain any quantity of controlled stock at the new office under this exception.
choices.why: Incorrect. The absence of controlled-substance supplies is an express condition.

choices.text: The exception automatically satisfies all Massachusetts registration requirements.
choices.why: Incorrect. Federal and state requirements must be assessed separately.

choices.text: The same exception applies automatically to an office in another state.
choices.why: Incorrect. The exception requires the other registered location to be in the same state.

questions.topic: Prescription issuance date versus future earliest-fill instruction
questions.trigger: A physician signs an otherwise valid paper Schedule II prescription on November 10 but dates the prescription November 24 to prevent early dispensing. The physician has a lawful electronic-prescribing exception. What should the physician do instead if using a qualifying multiple-prescription arrangement?
questions.legal_decision: Use the actual date of issuance and signing; put a separate lawful earliest-fill instruction on the prescription when applicable.
questions.critical_exception: An earliest-fill instruction is not the same as postdating the date of issuance.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the prescription were dated and signed on November 10 with a compliant earliest-fill instruction, this dating defect would not exist.
questions.stem: A physician signs an otherwise valid paper Schedule II prescription on November 10 but dates the prescription November 24 to prevent early dispensing. The physician has a lawful electronic-prescribing exception. What should the physician do instead if using a qualifying multiple-prescription arrangement?

choices.text: Leave the issuance date blank until the pharmacist fills it.
choices.why: Incorrect. The date is required at issuance.

choices.text: Permit the patient to select the issuance date after the visit.
choices.why: Incorrect. The prescriber must date the prescription on the issuance day.

choices.text: Date and sign the prescription on the actual issuance day and use the applicable separate earliest-fill instruction.
choices.why: Correct. The two dates serve distinct legal purposes.

choices.text: Use November 24 as the issuance date because the patient should not fill earlier.
choices.why: Incorrect. Federal law requires the prescription to be dated as of the day it is issued and signed.

choices.text: Write an ordinary refill instead of an earliest-fill instruction.
choices.why: Incorrect. Schedule II prescriptions may not be refilled.

critical_error_options.reason: Federal law requires the prescription to be dated as of the day it is issued and signed.

questions.topic: Initial vaccine training for pharmacist or pharmacy intern
questions.trigger: A pharmacy intern is preparing to begin vaccine administration under Policy 2023-02. The intern has current CPR and pharmacist supervision. Which initial ACPE-accredited course components are required by the pharmacist/intern training provision? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
questions.legal_decision: 12 contact hours self-study with case studies/assessment, eight live hours with final exam, and hands-on injection assessment.
questions.critical_exception: The technician six-hour pathway is not the pharmacist/intern pathway.
questions.counterfactual_flip: An intern who has completed only the technician curriculum has not met the specified intern training requirement.
questions.stem: A pharmacy intern is preparing to begin vaccine administration under Policy 2023-02. The intern has current CPR and pharmacist supervision. Which initial ACPE-accredited course components are required by the pharmacist/intern training provision? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: The technician-specific six-hour course alone.
choices.why: Incorrect. That is not the initial pharmacist/intern course requirement.

choices.text: Only current CPR certification, without the ACPE-accredited course.
choices.why: Incorrect. CPR is additional to the required course.

choices.text: Eight contact hours of live seminar with final exam.
choices.why: Correct. This is the stated live component.

choices.text: Twelve contact hours of self-study modules including case studies and assessment.
choices.why: Correct. This is the stated self-study component.

choices.text: Hands-on assessment of appropriate intramuscular and subcutaneous injection techniques.
choices.why: Correct. The policy includes the practical assessment.

questions.topic: COVID vaccine prior-dose verification recommendation versus reporting
questions.trigger: A qualified pharmacist plans an indicated COVID-19 vaccine administration under a valid order. The pharmacist has reliable documentation of the patient's prior COVID-19 formulation and dates in an EHR. Under the September 2025 vaccine policy, which statements correctly distinguish pre-administration review and post-administration reporting? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
questions.legal_decision: Prior COVID vaccine formulation and date confirmation is recommended and may use the EHR; vaccination information must be reported to MIIS.
questions.critical_exception: The general mandatory pre-administration MIIS review excludes COVID-19, but that does not remove post-vaccination reporting.
questions.counterfactual_flip: For a non-influenza, non-COVID vaccine, the general pre-administration MIIS review requirement applies.
questions.stem: A qualified pharmacist plans an indicated COVID-19 vaccine administration under a valid order. The pharmacist has reliable documentation of the patient's prior COVID-19 formulation and dates in an EHR. Under the September 2025 vaccine policy, which statements correctly distinguish pre-administration review and post-administration reporting? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Using the EHR for prior-dose confirmation eliminates the MIIS reporting duty.
choices.why: Incorrect. The reporting requirement is separate.

choices.text: The general rule mandates a pre-administration MIIS search for every COVID dose regardless of other sources.
choices.why: Incorrect. The general mandatory lookup provision excludes COVID-19.

choices.text: Prior formulation confirmation is forbidden because it is not mandatory.
choices.why: Incorrect. The policy recommends the confirmation.

choices.text: The vaccination information must be reported to MIIS after administration.
choices.why: Correct. The reporting requirement applies to administered vaccines.

choices.text: The EHR is an acceptable source for the recommended confirmation of prior COVID doses.
choices.why: Correct. The policy lists the EHR among possible sources.

questions.topic: Measuring device recommendation versus dispensing a device
questions.trigger: A patient collecting a new oral liquid medication already has a suitable calibrated oral syringe at home. The pharmacist confirms that it is appropriate for the prescribed dose, recommends its use, and provides the required instructions. Which conclusion reflects the Massachusetts measuring-device rule?
questions.legal_decision: Dispensing or recommending a proper measuring device is sufficient for this specific requirement.
questions.critical_exception: The rule does not mandate selling or supplying a new device if an appropriate device is recommended.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If no proper device were dispensed or recommended, the measuring-device requirement would not be satisfied.
questions.stem: A patient collecting a new oral liquid medication already has a suitable calibrated oral syringe at home. The pharmacist confirms that it is appropriate for the prescribed dose, recommends its use, and provides the required instructions. Which conclusion reflects the Massachusetts measuring-device rule?

choices.text: The pharmacist should recommend an ordinary household spoon in place of a suitable calibrated syringe.
choices.why: Incorrect. The requirement is for a proper device, not an unsuitable substitute.

choices.text: A new device must always be sold with every liquid prescription.
choices.why: Incorrect. The provision permits dispensing or recommending a proper measuring device.

choices.text: The recommendation of the confirmed suitable syringe satisfies this particular requirement.
choices.why: Correct. The rule expressly permits a recommendation.

choices.text: The measuring-device rule applies only to federally controlled liquids.
choices.why: Incorrect. The requirement addresses liquid medications generally.

choices.text: The pharmacy may omit all device discussion because the patient has used liquids before.
choices.why: Incorrect. A proper measuring device must be dispensed or recommended.

questions.topic: MassHealth unit-dose return excluded by third-party payment
questions.trigger: A nursing facility discontinues a listed MassHealth unit-dose drug. The package is intact, appropriately stored, within the required expiration and return deadlines, and meets the minimum quantity. Another insurer paid part of the original prescription. What is the appropriate conclusion about return for credit to MassHealth under 130 CMR 456.621?
questions.legal_decision: The unit-dose drug is excluded from the return-for-credit program when other insurance paid part or all.
questions.critical_exception: Physical return eligibility conditions do not override the third-party-payment exclusion.
questions.counterfactual_flip: Without other-insurance payment and with all other requirements satisfied, the return rule could require return for credit.
questions.stem: A nursing facility discontinues a listed MassHealth unit-dose drug. The package is intact, appropriately stored, within the required expiration and return deadlines, and meets the minimum quantity. Another insurer paid part of the original prescription. What is the appropriate conclusion about return for credit to MassHealth under 130 CMR 456.621?

choices.text: Treat the drug as automatically eligible for resale to any patient.
choices.why: Incorrect. The return program does not establish unrestricted redispensing authority.

choices.text: It is excluded from this return-for-credit program because another insurer paid part of the prescription.
choices.why: Correct. The exclusion covers both partial and full payment by other insurance.

choices.text: Return it for MassHealth credit because the package is intact.
choices.why: Incorrect. The other-insurance payment exclusion applies despite intact packaging.

choices.text: Return it for credit unless the other insurer paid the entire prescription.
choices.why: Incorrect. Partial third-party payment is sufficient for the exclusion.

choices.text: Return it for MassHealth credit solely because it is on Appendix F.
choices.why: Incorrect. Listing does not override the explicit exclusion.

questions.topic: HIPAA oral request to suspend accounting of disclosures
questions.trigger: A law enforcement official orally informs a covered pharmacy that giving a patient an accounting of a qualifying law-enforcement disclosure would be reasonably likely to impede the investigation and requests a temporary suspension. No written statement has yet been received. What must the pharmacy do under HIPAA? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
questions.legal_decision: Document the oral statement and official identity; temporarily suspend the relevant accounting right for no more than 30 days absent a qualifying written statement.
questions.critical_exception: An oral statement does not justify indefinite suspension or suspension of unrelated access rights.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A qualifying written statement received within the 30 days may specify a further suspension period.
questions.stem: A law enforcement official orally informs a covered pharmacy that giving a patient an accounting of a qualifying law-enforcement disclosure would be reasonably likely to impede the investigation and requests a temporary 45-day suspension. No written statement has yet been received. What must the pharmacy do under HIPAA? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Temporarily suspend accounting of the disclosures subject to the statement.
choices.why: Correct. The rule requires a limited suspension for the affected disclosures.

choices.text: Document the oral statement and the identity of the official.
choices.why: Correct. The oral-statement procedure requires that documentation.

choices.text: Permanently deny accounting of all disclosures based solely on the oral statement.
choices.why: Incorrect. The oral route is temporary and limited in scope.

choices.text: Automatically deny every request for access to the patient's own designated record set.
choices.why: Incorrect. This provision concerns the accounting right, not a blanket denial of access.

choices.text: Limit an oral-only suspension to no more than 30 days unless a qualifying written statement is received.
choices.why: Correct. The regulation establishes that cap for the oral route.

questions.topic: Documented good-faith refusal of unverified interstate controlled prescription
questions.trigger: A pharmacist receives an otherwise apparently valid Schedule IV prescription from an authorized out-of-state practitioner. Despite documented good-faith attempts, the pharmacist cannot obtain the additional verification required by Massachusetts law. The patient threatens to sue unless the pharmacy fills it. Which conclusion is most accurate?
questions.legal_decision: Do not fill; the statute provides protection from liability for refusing when required verification cannot be obtained after documented good-faith efforts.
questions.critical_exception: The liability protection does not authorize dispensing an unverified prescription.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the required verification succeeds and all other requirements are met, the verification barrier would be removed.
questions.stem: A pharmacist receives an otherwise apparently valid Schedule IV prescription from an authorized out-of-state practitioner. Despite documented good-faith attempts, the pharmacist cannot obtain the additional verification required by Massachusetts law. The patient threatens to sue unless the pharmacy fills it. Which conclusion is most accurate?

choices.text: Ask a cashier to certify authenticity based solely on the patient's account.
choices.why: Incorrect. That does not establish the required pharmacist verification.

choices.text: Refuse to fill and preserve the documented good-faith verification efforts.
choices.why: Correct. The statute prohibits filling and expressly addresses liability for this documented refusal.

choices.text: Dispense because the patient accepts personal responsibility.
choices.why: Incorrect. Patient consent does not replace statutory verification.

choices.text: Refuse without documenting any verification attempts and claim the specific statutory protection automatically.
choices.why: Incorrect. The protection is conditioned on documented good-faith efforts.

choices.text: Dispense because the patient's threat establishes a hardship exception.
choices.why: Incorrect. The statute does not waive the authenticity verification requirement on that basis.

critical_error_options.reason: Patient consent does not replace statutory verification.
The statute does not waive the authenticity verification requirement on that basis.

questions.topic: Automated initial EPCS transfer accuracy and record retention
questions.trigger: Two retail pharmacies complete an otherwise lawful initial electronic transfer of an unfilled Schedule IV prescription at the patient's request. Their software automatically populates the transfer fields. The receiving pharmacist discovers an incorrect transferring-pharmacist name in the transfer documentation; the prescription content itself is unchanged. A records manager also asks how long the transfer documentation must be kept under the federal initial-transfer rule. Which statements are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
questions.legal_decision: Ensure the automated information is complete and accurate; both pharmacies must retain electronic transfer records for two years from the transfer date under the federal rule.
questions.critical_exception: The initial EPCS transfer retention rule differs from the refill transfer record rule; automation does not remove pharmacist verification.
questions.counterfactual_flip: Accurately populated fields may be used in lieu of manual entry, but the retention obligation remains.
questions.stem: Two retail pharmacies complete an otherwise lawful initial electronic transfer of an unfilled Schedule IV prescription at the patient's request. Their software automatically populates the transfer fields. The receiving pharmacist discovers an incorrect transferring-pharmacist name in the transfer documentation; the prescription content itself is unchanged. A records manager also asks how long the transfer documentation must be kept under the federal initial-transfer rule. Which statements are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: The applicable pharmacist must ensure the automatically populated transfer documentation is accurate and complete.
choices.why: Correct. The automation provision assigns that responsibility to the applicable pharmacist.

choices.text: All automatically populated fields are exempt from pharmacist review.
choices.why: Incorrect. The accuracy and completeness requirement expressly applies to automated documentation.

choices.text: Both pharmacies must keep the initial electronic transfer records for two years from the transfer date under this federal rule.
choices.why: Correct. Section 1306.08(h) specifies both pharmacies and the transfer-date starting point.

choices.text: The transferring pharmacy may delete its transfer record once the receiving pharmacy confirms receipt.
choices.why: Incorrect. Both pharmacies must retain the electronic transfer records.

choices.text: The original prescription issue date should be replaced with the transfer date.
choices.why: Incorrect. A transfer does not authorize changing required prescription content.

questions.topic: MassPAT access when practitioner license suspended
questions.trigger: A practitioner has been using MassPAT for authorized purposes. The practitioner's relevant license is then suspended. The practitioner asks whether existing MassPAT authorization can remain active until the end of the current renewal period. Which answer reflects 105 CMR 700.012(F)?
questions.legal_decision: DPH must suspend access upon license or registration suspension; voiding or termination requires termination of access.
questions.critical_exception: Automatic authorization does not survive a qualifying suspension.
questions.counterfactual_flip: After lawful restoration, any reactivation must follow the applicable authorization process.
questions.stem: A practitioner has been using MassPAT for authorized purposes. The practitioner's relevant license is then suspended. The practitioner asks whether existing MassPAT authorization can remain active until the end of the current renewal period. Which answer reflects 105 CMR 700.012(F)?

choices.text: The practitioner automatically receives unrestricted public access instead.
choices.why: Incorrect. PMP data remain confidential and access is restricted.

choices.text: The account may be used through a delegate to avoid the suspension.
choices.why: Incorrect. Delegate access does not bypass suspended practitioner authorization.

choices.text: DPH must suspend the practitioner's PMP access.
choices.why: Correct. The regulation specifically provides for suspension of access.

choices.text: Access must continue until the practitioner's next renewal.
choices.why: Incorrect. The suspension triggers suspension of PMP access.

choices.text: Only a criminal conviction may affect an existing PMP account.
choices.why: Incorrect. License or registration suspension is an express trigger.

critical_error_options.reason: Delegate access does not bypass suspended practitioner authorization.

questions.topic: Practitioner requests Schedule II partial fill after issuance
questions.trigger: After issuing a valid nonemergency Schedule II prescription, the prescribing practitioner consults with the pharmacist and lawfully authorizes a partial fill of that prescription. The prescription remains within its allowable time period, and all state-law requirements are satisfied. Which additional entries are required for this subsequent practitioner request? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
questions.legal_decision: Document subsequent practitioner authorization, practitioner name, discussion date/time and pharmacist initials; retain applicable dispensing records.
questions.critical_exception: The subsequent consultation pathway differs from a partial quantity specified when the prescription was originally issued.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the prescriber specified the partial quantity at issuance, the separate subsequent-discussion notation would not be triggered.
questions.stem: After issuing a valid nonemergency Schedule II prescription, the prescribing practitioner consults with the pharmacist and lawfully authorizes a partial fill of that prescription. The prescription remains within its allowable time period, and all state-law requirements are satisfied. Which additional entries are required for this subsequent practitioner request? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Replace the original issuance date with the consultation date.
choices.why: Incorrect. A later consultation does not restart the issuance-based validity period.

choices.text: Maintain the applicable record of each partial dispensing.
choices.why: Correct. The dispensing record requirements continue to apply.

choices.text: Record the date and time of the discussion and the pharmacist's initials.
choices.why: Correct. These are expressly required additional elements.

choices.text: Record that the practitioner authorized the partial fill and identify the practitioner.
choices.why: Correct. The subsequent request requires the authorization notation and practitioner's name.

choices.text: Document the request as patient-initiated even though it was made by the prescriber.
choices.why: Incorrect. The record must accurately identify the practitioner request.

questions.topic: Institutional Schedule III-V label exception quantity threshold
questions.trigger: An institutional pharmacy dispenses a Schedule IV medication for staff administration to an institutionalized patient. All safeguards, records and identification-system conditions in 21 CFR 1306.24(c) are met; the medication is not possessed by the patient before administration. The proposed one-time supply is 30 days totaling 120 dosage units. Can the federal exception to ordinary package labeling apply to that supply?
questions.legal_decision: No; the exception allows no more than 34 days or 100 dosage units, whichever is less.
questions.critical_exception: Both the days and dosage-unit ceiling matter.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A supply of 25 days and 100 units could meet the federal quantity condition if the other requirements were met.
questions.stem: An institutional pharmacy dispenses a Schedule IV medication for staff administration to an institutionalized patient. All safeguards, records and identification-system conditions in 21 CFR 1306.24(c) are met; the medication is not possessed by the patient before administration. The proposed one-time supply is 30 days totaling 120 dosage units. Can the federal exception to ordinary package labeling apply to that supply?

choices.text: No, because 120 dosage units exceeds the 100-unit ceiling.
choices.why: Correct. The lesser of the two limits controls.

choices.text: Yes, if the pharmacy simply calls the supply a single unit.
choices.why: Incorrect. The actual dosage-unit count controls.

choices.text: Yes, because the supply is less than 34 days regardless of unit count.
choices.why: Incorrect. The 100-unit ceiling also applies.

choices.text: Yes, because any institutional patient qualifies automatically.
choices.why: Incorrect. The exception has specific quantity and other conditions.

choices.text: No, because the exception is limited to Schedule II.
choices.why: Incorrect. The cited provision covers Schedule III–V.

questions.topic: Child-resistant packaging exemption for potassium unit doses
questions.trigger: A pharmacist dispenses prescription potassium supplements in individually packaged unit doses. Product X contains 40 mEq of potassium per unit dose and Product Y contains 60 mEq per unit dose. Both are otherwise subject to the federal prescription special-packaging rule, and no purchaser or prescriber waiver applies. Which statement is correct about the specific potassium exemption?
questions.legal_decision: X meets the unit-dose potassium exemption; Y exceeds its 50 mEq per-unit limit.
questions.critical_exception: The exemption is formulation and per-unit quantity specific.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If Y contained no more than 50 mEq per unit dose, it could meet this exemption.
questions.stem: A pharmacist dispenses prescription potassium supplements in individually packaged unit doses. Product X contains 40 mEq of potassium per unit dose and Product Y contains 60 mEq per unit dose. Both are otherwise subject to the federal prescription special-packaging rule, and no purchaser or prescriber waiver applies. Which statement is correct about the specific potassium exemption?

choices.text: X qualifies for the specific exemption, but Y exceeds its limit.
choices.why: Correct. The unit-dose threshold is no more than 50 mEq of potassium.

choices.text: Only potassium dispensed as an OTC medicine can qualify under this specific prescription exemption.
choices.why: Incorrect. The cited provision expressly contains the prescription-drug exemption.

choices.text: Y qualifies because the higher strength is more concentrated.
choices.why: Incorrect. The higher per-unit quantity exceeds the exemption.

choices.text: Neither product meets the exemption because all prescription potassium requires special packaging.
choices.why: Incorrect. A qualifying unit-dose potassium exemption exists.

choices.text: Both products meet the exemption because both are unit-dose products.
choices.why: Incorrect. The exemption has a per-unit potassium limit.

questions.topic: Single small pseudoephedrine package logbook exception
questions.trigger: A customer purchases one sales package containing a total of 60 mg of pseudoephedrine. No other package is purchased in that transaction. All other applicable federal and state sale conditions are satisfied. Which federal recordkeeping conclusion follows from 21 CFR 1314.30(a)?
questions.legal_decision: The single-package purchase falls within the specific logbook exception.
questions.critical_exception: The exception is for one package containing no more than 60 mg, not a general exemption from other sales restrictions.
questions.counterfactual_flip: Two separate 30 mg packages would not meet the single-sales-package condition.
questions.stem: A customer purchases one sales package containing a total of 60 mg of pseudoephedrine. No other package is purchased in that transaction. All other applicable federal and state sale conditions are satisfied. Which federal recordkeeping conclusion follows from 21 CFR 1314.30(a)?

choices.text: The threshold is 60 grams rather than 60 milligrams.
choices.why: Incorrect. The stated threshold is in milligrams.

choices.text: The exception extends to any number of packages if each contains 60 mg.
choices.why: Incorrect. The provision specifies one sales package.

choices.text: The exception applies to this single package containing no more than 60 mg.
choices.why: Correct. The purchase satisfies the quantity and package conditions.

choices.text: The exception applies to one package containing any quantity.
choices.why: Incorrect. The package must contain no more than 60 mg.

choices.text: Every other applicable placement and sales restriction is automatically waived.
choices.why: Incorrect. The provision addresses logbook recordkeeping, not all restrictions.

questions.topic: CSOS electronic order cannot be endorsed to another supplier
questions.trigger: A pharmacy submits a valid electronically signed Schedule II controlled-substance order to Supplier A. Supplier A cannot fill it and wants to endorse that same electronic order to an unrelated Supplier B. Which action complies with the federal electronic-order rule?
questions.legal_decision: Supplier A may not endorse the electronic order to another supplier; the purchaser must arrange a lawful new order.
questions.critical_exception: The electronic-order prohibition is distinct from the rules for processing orders within a supplier's own registered locations.
questions.counterfactual_flip: Central processing within the same supplier's authorized registered network is governed by the separate §1305.22(a) conditions.
questions.stem: A pharmacy submits a valid electronically signed Schedule II controlled-substance order to Supplier A. Supplier A cannot fill it and wants to endorse that same electronic order to an unrelated Supplier B. Which action complies with the federal electronic-order rule?

choices.text: Transfer the purchaser's digital certificate to Supplier B.
choices.why: Incorrect. The electronic order and signature authority cannot be reassigned that way.

choices.text: Endorse the electronic order to Supplier B if both suppliers are DEA registered.
choices.why: Incorrect. The prohibition applies even when the other supplier is registered.

choices.text: Do not endorse the order to Supplier B; arrange a lawful order from the purchaser.
choices.why: Correct. Section 1305.23 prohibits endorsement of electronic orders to another supplier.

choices.text: Convert the electronic order to a paper copy and endorse it as an executed Form 222.
choices.why: Incorrect. A printout is not a newly executed valid paper order.

choices.text: Endorse it whenever the purchaser gives verbal permission.
choices.why: Incorrect. Verbal permission does not override the electronic-order rule.

questions.topic: Actual receipt date for controlled stock records
questions.trigger: A wholesale packing slip for controlled stock is dated November 12, the supplier ships the order November 13, and the pharmacy actually receives and accepts it November 15. Which date must the pharmacy use as the date of receipt in its controlled-substance record?
questions.legal_decision: Record the actual receipt date, November 15.
questions.critical_exception: Invoice and shipment dates do not replace the actual receipt date.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the stock actually arrived November 13, that would be the receipt date.
questions.stem: A wholesale packing slip for controlled stock is dated November 12, the supplier ships the order November 13, and the pharmacy actually receives and accepts it November 15. Which date must the pharmacy use as the date of receipt in its controlled-substance record?

choices.text: November 12, the packing-slip date.
choices.why: Incorrect. The packing-slip creation date is not the actual receipt date.

choices.text: November 15, the actual receipt date.
choices.why: Correct. The rule requires recording the date the substances were actually received.

choices.text: November 13, the supplier's shipment date.
choices.why: Incorrect. Shipment and receipt are distinct events.

choices.text: The date of the pharmacy's next biennial inventory.
choices.why: Incorrect. The inventory date does not establish the receipt date.

choices.text: Any date chosen by the Manager of Record.
choices.why: Incorrect. The actual event date controls.

questions.topic: Controlled-substance access following DEA registration denial
questions.trigger: A pharmacy considers hiring a person for a stockroom job that includes access to controlled substances. The applicant has never been convicted of a felony, but a prior application by that individual for DEA registration was denied. No DEA waiver or other applicable exception is in place. Which action is consistent with the federal security rule?
questions.legal_decision: Do not employ the person in a position involving access to controlled substances under the stated circumstances.
questions.critical_exception: A prior DEA registration denial is an independent access restriction, not dependent on a controlled-substance felony.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A role without controlled-substance access must be assessed separately under other applicable law.
questions.stem: A pharmacy considers hiring a person for a stockroom job that includes access to controlled substances. The applicant has never been convicted of a felony, but a prior application by that individual for DEA registration was denied. No DEA waiver or other applicable exception is in place. Which action is consistent with the federal security rule?

choices.text: Conclude that federal law absolutely prohibits every job at any pharmacy regardless of access.
choices.why: Incorrect. The specified rule concerns employment or agency involving controlled-substance access.

choices.text: Assign the person to controlled stock only under remote camera monitoring.
choices.why: Incorrect. Monitoring does not remove the employment-access prohibition.

choices.text: Allow controlled-substance access because no felony conviction exists.
choices.why: Incorrect. A prior DEA registration denial is a separate listed ground.

choices.text: Do not assign employment involving controlled-substance access under these facts.
choices.why: Correct. The prior denial is independently covered by the security restriction.

choices.text: Allow access only to Schedule III–V controlled stock.
choices.why: Incorrect. The provision is not limited to Schedule II.

critical_error_options.reason: A prior DEA registration denial is a separate listed ground.

questions.topic: Specialty pharmacy delivery to retail pickup location
questions.actor: Specialty pharmacy and receiving retail pharmacy
questions.trigger: A specialty pharmacy proposes sending a patient-specific refrigerated prescription to a retail pharmacy for patient pickup. The specialty pharmacy intends to send the product in its final package; the retail staff plan to open and repackage it before pickup. According to the Massachusetts Board's Medication Delivery and Shipping advisory, which plan is consistent with the Board's recommendations?
questions.legal_decision: Deliver the final packaged product without alteration at the retail location and ensure the receiving location knows the special storage requirements.
questions.critical_exception: The question tests the Board's best-practice advisory, not an independent statutory mandate.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the retail site receives the final package without alteration and is informed of storage requirements, these particular recommendations are satisfied.
questions.stem: A specialty pharmacy proposes sending a patient-specific refrigerated prescription to a retail pharmacy for patient pickup. The specialty pharmacy intends to send the product in its final package; the retail staff plan to open and repackage it before pickup. According to the Massachusetts Board's Medication Delivery and Shipping advisory, which plan is consistent with the Board's recommendations?

choices.text: Allow retail staff to repackage the prescription whenever the patient requests pickup there.
choices.why: Incorrect. The advisory specifies no alteration at the receiving retail pharmacy.

choices.text: Send an unfinished product and let the receiving pharmacy complete its packaging.
choices.why: Incorrect. The advisory calls for delivery of the final packaged product.

choices.text: Send the final package, leave it unaltered at the receiving site, and communicate its special storage requirements.
choices.why: Correct. This reflects the advisory's recommendations for alternative-location delivery.

choices.text: Assume refrigeration instructions are unnecessary because both sites are pharmacies.
choices.why: Incorrect. The receiving location should be informed of any special storage needs.

choices.text: Treat the advisory as a blanket authorization to disregard other applicable dispensing and shipping laws.
choices.why: Incorrect. The advisory calls for compliance with applicable law and does not supersede it.

questions.citation: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy, Advisory: Medication Delivery and Shipping, revised January 9, 2025, Delivery to Alternative Locations

questions.topic: USP 797 competency of pharmacists who directly supervise without compounding
questions.trigger: A pharmacist directly oversees Category 2 sterile compounding personnel but does not personally prepare CSPs. Management proposes that the pharmacist receive no ongoing core-skills, garbing or aseptic manipulation evaluation because the pharmacist does not compound. Which conclusions are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
questions.legal_decision: Supervisory role requires applicable core skills and garbing initial/annual competency and at least annual aseptic manipulation evaluation for direct oversight.
questions.critical_exception: Not personally preparing CSPs is not a blanket exemption from evaluation; the evaluation reflects the oversight role.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A person with no direct oversight duties would be evaluated under the requirements applicable to that person's actual role.
questions.stem: A pharmacist directly oversees Category 2 sterile compounding personnel but does not personally prepare CSPs. Management proposes that the pharmacist receive no ongoing core-skills, garbing or aseptic manipulation evaluation because the pharmacist does not compound. Which conclusions are correct? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: A current pharmacist license by itself replaces all of the specified competency assessments.
choices.why: Incorrect. Licensure is not a substitute for required competency evaluation.

choices.text: Direct oversight requires aseptic manipulation evaluation at least every 12 months, appropriate to the activities overseen.
choices.why: Correct. The evaluation applies even if the pharmacist does not personally compound.

choices.text: Garbing competency must be assessed initially and at least every 12 months.
choices.why: Correct. The supervisory evaluation includes this competency.

choices.text: The supervising pharmacist must demonstrate applicable core skills initially and at least every 12 months.
choices.why: Correct. USP identifies this requirement for personnel who supervise compounding without personally compounding.

choices.text: The supervising pharmacist is entirely exempt from competency evaluation.
choices.why: Incorrect. USP distinguishes role-specific training from complete exemption.

critical_error_options.reason: USP distinguishes role-specific training from complete exemption.

questions.topic: Section 503A requirements for ingredients other than bulk drug substances
questions.trigger: A 503A pharmacy plans a lawful patient-specific compound using an eligible active ingredient with a valid certificate of analysis. A nonbulk inactive ingredient has an applicable USP/NF monograph. The proposed excipient does not meet the monograph standard. Which decision is appropriate for qualifying under section 503A?
questions.legal_decision: Use compliant nonbulk ingredients meeting applicable USP/NF standards and the compounding chapter; active ingredient compliance alone is insufficient.
questions.critical_exception: The statutory nonbulk-ingredient condition is separate from bulk active ingredient eligibility.
questions.counterfactual_flip: An excipient complying with its applicable monograph and other compounding standards would remove this particular defect.
questions.stem: A 503A pharmacy plans a lawful patient-specific compound using an eligible active ingredient with a valid certificate of analysis. A nonbulk inactive ingredient has an applicable USP/NF monograph. The proposed excipient does not meet the monograph standard. Which decision is appropriate for qualifying under section 503A?

choices.text: A patient-specific prescription overrides all monograph requirements.
choices.why: Incorrect. Patient specificity is necessary but does not remove ingredient requirements.

choices.text: Use the excipient because a valid active-ingredient certificate is sufficient for every ingredient.
choices.why: Incorrect. The nonbulk-ingredient standard applies independently.

choices.text: Replace it with an ingredient meeting applicable standards before claiming section 503A eligibility.
choices.why: Correct. Section 503A includes a separate condition for ingredients other than bulk drug substances.

choices.text: The pharmacy may label the excipient as a bulk ingredient to avoid compliance.
choices.why: Incorrect. Changing a description does not cure noncompliance.

choices.text: Use the excipient because it is pharmacologically inactive.
choices.why: Incorrect. Inactive status does not waive applicable ingredient quality requirements.

questions.topic: Board waiver petition must demonstrate substantive safeguards
questions.trigger: A licensed pharmacy seeks a waiver of a Board regulation eligible for waiver. The current Manager of Record submits a petition explaining that compliance is impractical and costly, but gives no public-interest justification and no alternative safeguards for patient safety. Which factors must the Board be able to find before granting the waiver? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
questions.legal_decision: Compelling public interest, impractical and unduly burdensome compliance, and sufficient public-health/welfare/safety safeguards.
questions.critical_exception: Cost alone is insufficient; the Board retains discretion and cannot waive a requirement where law prohibits doing so.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A complete petition demonstrating all three factors may be considered, but approval is not automatic.
questions.stem: A licensed pharmacy seeks a waiver of a Board regulation eligible for waiver. The current Manager of Record submits a petition explaining that compliance is impractical and costly, but gives no public-interest justification and no alternative safeguards for patient safety. Which factors must the Board be able to find before granting the waiver? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Sufficient safeguards would protect public health, welfare and safety without compliance with the waived requirement.
choices.why: Correct. The alternative safeguards are a necessary consideration.

choices.text: A compelling public interest would be served by granting the waiver.
choices.why: Correct. The regulation requires a public-interest finding.

choices.text: The pharmacy's request automatically grants the waiver when filed.
choices.why: Incorrect. The Board must act and determine that the criteria are satisfied.

choices.text: Adherence to the requirement would be impractical and unduly burdensome.
choices.why: Correct. This is another required finding.

choices.text: The Board may waive any state statute whenever the pharmacy would save money.
choices.why: Incorrect. The waiver authority concerns eligible Board regulations and is limited by law.
